how_to_run: From this folder: `python3 ../../framework-evals/run_eval.py <out-dir> [<eval-id>...] --evals evals.json [--tier core|regression|all] [--runs N] [--parallel N] [--skill-model MODEL] [--dry-run] [--yes]`. Each eval is tagged `tier` (build.md 13 and rules 14): core holds the routing and entry cases, the wrong place, the safety and fail-closed cases (the block, the wrapper, the read floor, the bare run, quick real checks, the older version, live changes, schedules, Microsoft 365's agent), the quote check and the first-time-leader journey on each platform; it gates the release and runs three times. Everything else is the regression suite. `spec_item` names the build.md 13 bullet each eval covers. The smaller-model round re-runs the evals marked `smaller_model_round: true` (routing, safety and fail-closed, the quote check) with `--skill-model` set to the smaller model, and the report gives each item's difference from the main model's round. `preconditions` name what a run needs that isn't true yet (release checks T19 verifies; fixture variants T71 regenerates); until then, read the eval's result against them. Fixtures are `dir:` folders in ../../framework-fixtures/ or names from fixtures/make_fixture.py (`--list`; `--check` builds each and prints its routing state). Without --yes the runner prints the cost estimate and stops. Validate edits with `python3 ../../framework-evals/validate_evals.py evals.json --build-fixtures --strict-tiers` and `python3 ../../framework-evals/check_quotes.py evals evals.json`. Effort is counted in leader actions, never time.
